content.title: Where is the Final Four being played this year? 2026 location, stadium
content.text: April 4, 2026, 3:30 p.m. ETThe final weekend of March Madness is here. So where is the Final Four this year?The Final Four being played at Lucas Oil Stadium in downtown Indianapolis, home of the Colts, on Saturday, April 4.There will be two games in Indianapolis on Saturday, with 3-seed Illinois facing 2-seed UConn in the first game with a 6:09 p.m. tipoff time, while Michigan basketball will play Arizona in the late game with a 8:54 p.m. scheduled tip time and to try to earn a spot in the national championship.Watch Final Four on Sling TVThe title game is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. Monday, April 6, with all three games in Indianapolis airing on TBS.Both games will be televised on TBS with streaming available on Sling TV. Where is the Final Four 2026?The Final Four has descended upon Indianapolis for three games this weekend, starting at 6:09 p.m. on Saturday with Illinois vs. UConn.This is the ninth time that Indianapolis has hosted the Final Four and the sixth time this century, with the most recent being in 2021 when Baylor topped Gonzaga in the national title game. What time does the Final Four start?The first game of the day will begin at 6:09 p.m. for Illinois vs. UConn, with Michigan and Arizona starting about 25 minutes after the first game ends.First game time: 6:09 p.m. ET.Date: Saturday, April 4.Location: Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis. What time is Michigan vs Arizona in March Madness Final FourTime: Approximately 8:54 p.m. ET.Date: Saturday, April 4.Location: Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis. What channel is the Final Four on?Channel: TBS.Tipoff: 6:09 p.m. ET for Game 1, approximately 8:54 p.m. ET for Game 2.Streaming: Sling TV.Audio: Westwood One Sports.Saturday's Final Four matchups between Illinois and UConn and Michigan and Arizona can be watched on TBS, TNT and truTV, with streaming available on Sling TV and HBO Max.Watch the Final Four on Sling TV Final Four picks, predictionsMichigan vs ArizonaTony Garcia, Detroit Free Press: It's not Muhammad Ali vs. Joe Frazier, but it will be a heavyweight battle. Michigan and Arizona both bulldozed their way through their respective regionals, all setting up this moment. The Wildcats are one of the few teams that have the size, depth and skill that can match the Wolverines at every spot. But Michigan players and coaches say they're back to their Las Vegas level – assistant Justin Joyner said it started in the second half of the Saint Louis matchup. Michigan has felt all year if it plays it's A-game, it can beat anyone in the country. Arizona will certainly put that to the test. But this Michigan team, led by Yaxel Lendeborg who's had his best month of the season, is on a mission. The pick: Michigan 86, Arizona 83.Illinois vs UConnAndrew Birkle, Detroit Free Press: Illinois has the more free-flowing offense and as backed up its status as an analytics darling by making it to Indianapolis for its first Final Four under Brad Underwood, but at this point, how do you bet against Dan Hurley in March? After surviving a Michigan State comeback in the second half of the Sweet 16, UConn showed its championship pedigree with an epic comeback of its own, topped off by a Braylon Mullins buzzer-beater that'll be showed for years to come. Illinois gets off to a strong start but UConn is fueled with confidence from its run to Indy and once again finds a way to win to get back to the title game for the third time in four years. The pick: UConn 69, Illinois 66. Final Four announcersPlay-by-play: Ian Eagle.Analysts: Grant Hill, Bill Raftery.Sideline reporter: Tracy Wolfson.It's no surprise CBS will have its A-crew in Indianapolis for all three games this weekend as we determine the national champion in 2026. This is Eagle's third Final Four after taking over for longtime play-by-play man Jim Nantz.Need to catch up on the news during your lunch break?
